Two drivers, one frame

The same colour negative on the same OpticFilm 8200i, scanned once with our plustek8200i backend and once with upstream SANE's genesys GL128. Both are shown through the identical negative-conversion pipeline, so what you see differs only because the scanners' raw data differs.

1 · Whole frame, 600 dpi

Both scans are drawn on one shared film coordinate system, so the same piece of film lies in the same place in every view. Dark areas are where a backend's scan window did not reach. White areas are inside a window but beyond the film (unexposed film inverts to white).

2 · Scan area

Distance in millimetres between the film's edge and the edge of each backend's scan window. A negative number means film was cut off.

600 dpileftrighttopbottom
ours+0.13+0.80+1.65+1.44
genesys+1.19−0.25+0.25+0.38
3600 dpi
ours+0.17+0.85+1.64+1.56
genesys+1.19+0.06+0.45+0.22
What this means. Genesys's window sits 1.06 mm to the left of ours, a constant at both resolutions. It leaves a 1.2 mm dark strip on the left and runs up against the film's right edge. Its top and bottom margins are only 0.2–0.45 mm and drift with resolution (ours stay at ~1.6 mm), so a small positioning error would clip the picture. Copying genesys's horizontal offset would move our window toward clipping; ours is the safer set of values.

3 · Detail at 3600 dpi

The same physical area cut from each 3600 dpi scan (1000×750 pixels, shown at the full width of the box), lined up to within a few pixels. Drag to wipe between them.

oursgenesys

The girl's face and a tulip

oursgenesys

The large, soft-focus tulip on the right

oursgenesys

Flowers and soil at the bottom

Sharpness is a wash; colour is not. At full resolution both backends resolve the same detail, and even the dust specks line up. The visible difference is colour balance: genesys's raw data renders greener and brighter. That comes from each backend's calibration (white balance and exposure of the raw data), not from lost detail, and it is a matter of per-channel gain that can be balanced in software. Our infrared channel, which can remove those dust specks, is not available through genesys at all.

How this was made. Same frame, same film holder position, scanned on 2026-10-09 with an OpticFilm 8200i (USB 07b3:1825). Ours: plustek8200i from this repository. Genesys: upstream SANE master (415217c5) with its GL128 command set. Both raw 16-bit scans went through the same nv-cli render negative conversion with each backend's own film-base estimate, no dust removal. The two images were aligned by correlating edges; the whole-frame views use the measured offset (1.06 mm horizontal, 1.44 mm vertical at 600 dpi). Single scanner, single frame.

Where to go next. The backend, build instructions and the scripts that produced these images live in the OpticFilm8200i-sane repository. Upstreaming is tracked in SANE backends work item #886.
